THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING, THIS DAY,
VIJAYKUMAR A. PATIL J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Challenging the order dated 31.08.2021 in LAC No.76/2015 on the file of the Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Mysuru, respondent No.2 in the said case has preferred this appeal.
2. The appellant was respondent No.2, respondent No.1 was the petitioner and respondent No.2 was respondent No.1 before the Trial Court.
The parties are referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the Trial Court.
3. Brief facts leading to filing of this appeal are that the State Government acquired land measuring 1 acre 35 guntas in Sy.No.99/P56 of Yalachahalli Village, Yelwala Hobli, Mysuru District.
The Land Acquisition Officer determined the market value of the land at Rs.36,50,000/- per acre.
The Land Acquisition Officer found that there is a serious dispute with regard to title amongst the respondents.
He made a reference NC: 2024:KHC:26997-DB under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') by depositing a sum of Rs.68,43,750/-.
4. Respondents entered appearance before the Trial Court and filed the objections.
Respondent No.1 examined himself as RW-1 whereas respondent No.2 examined himself as RW-2 and on their behalf Exs.R1 to R28 were marked.

The Trial Court on hearing the parties, ordered that respondent No.1 is solely entitled for the entire compensation amount deposited by the petitioner.
5.

Sri.Vyshak P.N., learned counsel appearing for Sri.Ajit P.B., learned counsel for the appellant /
respondent No.2 submits that one Nagegowda and others entered into an agreement of sale dated 14.08.2006 in favour of respondent No.2.
However, he did not come forward to execute the sale deed despite receipt of the substantial amount.
Hence, respondent No.2 filed O.S.No.698/2013 seeking relief of specific performance of contract.
The said suit came to be decreed on 01.01.2014.
Respondent No.2 filed execution petition in Ex.P.No.390/2014 and thereafter obtained the sale deed from the Court and got registered on 29.12.2014.
Pursuant to the said registered sale deed, respondent No.2 being the absolute owner of the acquired land is entitled for the compensation amount deposited before the Court.

It is submitted that respondent No.2 came to know that respondent No.1 had obtained registered sale deed dated 11.11.2013 and upon enquiry, they came to know that respondent No.1 Mr. Chandrashekar vs Special Land Acquisition Officer on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126980396/
2 filed a suit in O.S.No.403/2009 by suppressing the material facts.

sentences.text: The said suit came to be decreed on 12.12.2011.
It is further submitted that the judgment and decree dated 12.12.2011 in O.S.No.403/2009 was confirmed in RSA No.400/2013.

It is also submitted that respondent No.2 filed O.S.No.596/2016 seeking declaration that judgment and decree passed in O.S.No.403/2009 and registered sale deed dated 03.01.2014 are null and void and not binding on respondent No.2 over the suit schedule property.
The said suit came to be dismissed.

Being aggrieved by the same,
respondent No.2 filed RFA No.1148/2021 which is pending consideration before this Court.
It is argued that till the appeal filed by the respondent No.2 is decided, this appeal cannot be adjudicated.
Hence, he seeks to defer the consideration of this appeal till the disposal of RFA No.1148/2021.

Per contra, Sri.H.L.Pradeep Kumar, learned counsel for respondent No.1 herein / SLAO submits that he is a formal party in the present proceedings and he seeks to pass appropriate orders based on the evidence available on record.
7. Sri

.Y.K.Narayana Sharma, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 herein / respondent No.1 supports the impugned judgment and decree of the Trial Court and submits that the suit filed by respondent No.2 in O.S.No.596/2016 is dismissed.

It is submitted that this Court in RFA No.1148/2021 declined to grant stay as prayed by respondent No.2 by permitting respondent No.1 to withdraw the amount in deposit before the Reference Court by furnishing security to the satisfaction of the Reference Court and the money is withdrawn subject to result of the said appeal.
He submits that in view of the said facts, this appeal does not survive.
It is further submitted that respondent No.2 has failed to establish his title over the property.
The Trial Court has recorded detailed finding with regard to the various proceedings between the parties and ordered to release the compensation amount in favour of respondent No.1.
Hence, he seeks dismissal of the appeal.

Considering the submissions of both sides and on examining the materials on record, the point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether the impugned judgment and decree calls for any interference"?
ANALYSIS

9. The subject matter of the present proceedings is the land measuring 1 acre 35 guntas in Sy.No.99/P56 of Yalachahalli Village, Yelwala Hobli, Mysuru District which was acquired by the State Government for public purpose.
The Land Acquisition Officer determined the market value of the land at Rs.36,50,000/- per acre.
The Land Acquisition Officer found that there is a serious dispute with regard to title amongst the respondents.
Hence, he made a reference under Section 30 of the Act by depositing a sum of Rs.68,43,750/- before the Reference Court.

sentences.text: Originally, the subject land was owned by Sri.Nagegowda and others.
The said Nagegowda entered into an agreement of sale with respondent No.1 on 01.09.2006.

Thereafter, he did not come forward to execute the sale deed in NC: 2024:KHC:26997-DB favour of respondent No.1 which compelled the respondent No.1 to file O.S.No.403/2009 seeking the relief of specific performance of contract against said Nagegowda and others.
The IV Addl. Sr. Civil Judge and JMFC, Mysuru decreed the said suit on 12.12.2011.
Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree, the said Nagegowda and others filed R.A.No.69/2012.
The V Addl. District Judge, Mysuru vide judgment dated 18.01.2013 dismissed the appeal.
Being aggrieved by both the judgments of the Trial Court and the learned Appellate Court, the said Nagegowda and others filed RSA No.400/2013.
This Court, vide judgment and decree dated 11.06.2013, dismissed RSA No.400/2013.
After the dismissal of the said second appeal, respondent No.1 filed Ex.P.No.679/2014 to execute the judgment and decree of the Trial Court.
The Execution Court appointed the Court Commissioner to execute the sale deed in favour of respondent No.1 and accordingly, sale deed as per Ex-R18 was registered on 11.11.2013.
Subsequently, possession of the property was delivered pursuant to the delivery warrant issued by the Execution Court.

11. The material available on record indicates that the said Nagegowda and others said to have executed another NC: 2024:KHC:26997-DB agreement of sale in favour of respondent No.2 and did not execute sale deed in favour of the appellant.
Hence, respondent No.2 filed O.S.No.698/2013 before the III Addl.
Senior
Civil Judge and JMFC, Mysuru, seeking relief of specific performance of contract
and the said suit came to be decreed on 01.01.2014.
Respondent No.2, to execute the said decree, filed Ex.case No.390/2014.
Respondent No.2 got the sale deed registered on 29.12.2014 pursuant to the orders of the Execution Court.

12. The materials available on record further indicate that on coming to know about the agreement of sale executed by Nagegowda and others in favour of respondent No.1, about various proceedings between respondent No.1 and Nagegowda and others and registration of sale deed through Court in favour of respondent No.1, filed O.S.No.596/2016 seeking relief of declaration that the judgment and decree passed in O.S.No.403/2009 dated 12.12.2011 is not binding on respondent No.2 and consequently to declare that the registered sale deed in respect of suit schedule property in Ex.No.168/2012 dated 03.01.2014 in favour of respondent No.1 is null and void and not binding on the rights of NC: 2024:KHC:26997-DB respondent no.2 over the suit schedule property.
Respondent No.2 herein was defendant No.1 in the said suit.
The Trial Court, considering the evidence available on record, dismissed the suit.
Respondent No.2, being aggrieved by the dismissal of O.S.No.596/2016, preferred RFA No.1148/2021 which is pending consideration before this Court.
This Court in RFA No.1148/2021 permitted respondent No.1 to withdraw the amount in deposit before the Reference Court on furnishing security to the said amount.
13. The original suit in O.S.No.403/2009 filed by respondent No.1 has attained finality.
RSA No.400/2013 filed by the original owner has been dismissed by this Court by confirming the judgment and decree of the Trial Court and the 1st Appellate Court.

After dismissal of the regular second appeal, the Execution Court ordered execution of sale deed in favour of respondent No.1 through the process of Court and sale deed dated 11.11.2013 was registered in the office of Sub- Registrar, Mysuru.

sentences.text: The regular first appeal filed by respondent No.2 is pending before this Court - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:26997-DB and unless respondent No.2 succeeds in the said appeal, he cannot have any right over the acquired property or the compensation.
It is always open for respondent No.2 to proceed in accordance with law if he succeeds in RFA No.1148/2021.
In RFA No.1148/2021, no interim stay is granted and by virtue of the interim order in the said appeal, compensation is released to respondent No.1 subject to result of the said appeal.
Since the said order has attained finality, nothing survives in this appeal.
14. Parties are bound by the ultimate judgment in RFA No.1148/2021.

Hence, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Appeal is dismissed.
No order as to costs.
